propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when a model id contains a colon in its version suffix (canonical Bedrock form `...-v1:0`), causing _resolve_target to return the bare model instead of the provider-qualified target
The decision to treat `:` in a model string as a provider separator fails for Bedrock canonical ids where the colon is part of the model id itself, not a qualifier separator
An explicitly configured provider must be checked first before scanning the model string for qualifiers, so no punctuation in a model id can overrule or silently drop an explicit instruction

Two independent implementations of the qualification decision (_resolve_target and infer_provider) can drift apart; they must route through a single shared function to prevent the same defect from manifesting through different code paths

A bare unqualified model id with no configured provider should still infer a provider by name (back-compat), while a conflicting configured-provider / inline-qualifier pair should raise rather than silently pick a winner
